# Independent SystemOne wire fixtures

These files precede the G04 implementation. They contain invented customer text,
numeric examples and artifact claims. They are not outputs of either transport,
trained model observations, customer data or evidence that a server loaded a model.
The repeated-digit hashes in `artifact-attestation.json` are synthetic claims;
even that complete object must never become an observed self-hosted qualification.

The independent expected mapping uses the published `POST /v1/systemone` body
and raw response shape. Choice options and score levels become `criteria`;
Noul's `noul` value becomes the existing logical `probability_true`. The ordered
score fixture has expectation 1. Its mass at the two outer levels distinguishes
the SGLang adapter's zero confidence from a reference top-probability statistic.
The Workers AI fixture deliberately has a different distribution and confidence.
Neither fixture establishes threshold portability or quality on a real workload.

Primary protocol sources read on 2026-10-19:

- [SGLang Clef cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Cloudflare/clef)
- [SGLang System One API](https://docs.sglang.io/docs/supported-models/decision_models#system-one-compatible-api)
- [Cloudflare Clef reference implementation](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef/blob/main/joint_schema_model.py)
- [System One HTTP reference](https://docs.system-one.dev/en/docs/api)

The upstream recipe, deployed artifact, effective context and confidence profile
must be pinned again for any separately authorized actual endpoint observation.
No endpoint, account, model process or GPU was exercised to create these fixtures.
